Online Safety in Singapore

Singapore’s Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025 (OSRAA) establishes new legal frameworks to protect individuals in Singapore from specified online harms and to provide victims with timely redress for certain categories of content.
Consistent with
, users on >x< are responsible for sharing only content that complies with applicable laws and that they are comfortable sharing publicly.

Below, we provide information on how Singapore-based users can enjoy a safe experience on >x<, including how to report content on >x< that they believe violates our Rules, is illegal or otherwise restricted under the applicable Singapore legal framework, as well as details regarding the appeal process.
User Controls

To help you enjoy a safe experience on >x<, we provide tools designed to help you to control what you see, so that you can personalize your experience on >x<. We make it easy for you to take action on a post. Tap the … icon at the top of any post on your timeline to quickly access options like unfollow, mute, block, report, and more.
Users can choose to either see or stop seeing someone’s posts on their timeline.
Users can mute an account if they do not want to see that account’s posts.

Block is a feature that helps you control how you interact with other accounts on >x<. This feature helps people in restricting specific accounts from following, Direct Messaging, and engaging with them.

Users can choose who can reply to their posts. The default setting for public accounts is that anyone can reply, but options are available to turn off replies entirely (except for mentioned accounts), limit replies to verified accounts, or limit replies to accounts that the posting user follows. A user can adjust these settings when composing a post, with their adjustments affecting that individual post. To help minimise unwanted replies and improve meaningful conversations, users can also adjust who can reply to a post after the post has been shared. Learn more about conversations on >x<
Users can report accounts or posts they think are in violation of the >x< Rules. More details can be found below.

We also provide tools to help you decide what others can see about you. This includes but is not limited to our discoverability settings, sharing your location in posts, and media settings which allow you to mark your posts as containing sensitive content.
The Singapore Online Safety Commission

The Singapore Online Safety Commission (OSC) supports the office of the Commissioner of Online Safety (the Commissioner), and is a dedicated government agency established under OSRAA to provide support to victims of harmful content.

Reporting Flow Process

Please complete all necessary information in the applicable forms, following the instructions, in order to submit the report. Upon submission, you will receive confirmation that your report was submitted. Your report will then be routed to the appropriate team, processed expeditiously in accordance with our obligations under applicable laws, and you will be notified of the outcome as soon as our team has all available information to make a final decision.

In the case of a report about content that is prohibited by >x< Rules, illegal and/or that >x< is legally required to restrict under the law, if a violation is identified, >x< will notify the violating account about the enforcement action and their right to appeal. >x< does not disclose information about the person who submitted the complaint.

Online Harm Notice Under OSRAA

OSRAA establishes a new legal framework which, in appropriate circumstances, may provide a basis for victims of certain types of online harm to seek remedies through the Singapore courts. For further information, please refer to the

>x< is in the process of establishing the appropriate method and channel for victims of specified online harms under OSRAA to be able to submit an Online Harm Notice to >x< for further action. Once available, to submit an Online Harm Notice to >x<, users must:
Use the prescribed form of notice, in the prescribed manner, setting out the prescribed particulars; and
Submit the duly populated form to >x< via the method and channel directed.
